why: I compared the builder brief with every PASS/FAIL condition and probe in the verifier brief. The builder brief has none of the verifier's probes. It doesn't include the scratch files (clean.jsonl, badmid.jsonl, torn.jsonl, blanks.jsonl) or their expected outputs like "<path>:2:". It also leaves out the `node --input-type=module -e` lint script, the "two bad rows" case, the grep/test -f commands and the mutation test. What it asks for are behaviour specs restated from the expect lines (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, torn last row checked, exit codes 0/1/2, package.json fields). It also tells the builder to write its own node:test tests for the five cases the expect line names, which is allowed. The commands it mentions (npm ci, npm test, waiting for the test workflow) are the repository's own tests or come from the expect lines, so those are allowed too. "Strip a trailing \r" is a coding instruction, not a probe. The criterion holds.
